findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a single use 2 oz cup stored in powdered sugar and cinnamon sugar. CORRECTED- the cup was removed and discarded. The person in charge (PIC) stated they are actively reminding employees to not use scoops without handles in ready to eat (RTE) foods. Ensure all RTE foods are handled with gloves, deli paper, or a scoop with a handle- to differentiate between the food contact and hand contact surface moving forward to prevent bare hand contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a food handler on shift with no Food Handler certificate available. All employees must have food handler who handle food must have certificates to be made available during inspections within 30 days of employment. Correct by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
SECOND REPEAT: The CFM has not completed Allergen Training. Complete training and test to be made available by the next routine inspection. Certified Food Protection Managers at high risk establishments must complete Allergen Awareness training and test within 30 days of employment, to be renewed every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

Ensure all ready to eat (RTE) foods are handled with gloves, deli paper, or a scoop with a handle- to differentiate between the food contact and hand contact surface moving forward to prevent bare hand contamination.

(B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed multiple soda nozzles in both the lobby and drive-thru to contain an accumulation of biofilm. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) removed the soda nozzles to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure soda nozzles are both cleaned AND sanitized each night to remove debris that could contaminate RTE beverages. Food contact surfaces must be maintained clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed unlabeled spray bottle beneath the front counter. The PIC verified that the substance was sanitizer. CORRECTED- the PIC labeled the container to display the contents. Ensure all chemicals are properly labeled to prevent food contamination.
findings.citation_text: 7-101.11 Identifying Information, Prominence. Containers of POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS and PERSONAL CARE ITEMS shall bear a legible manufacturer's label. [Pf]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspector observed white powder at the fry station to contain no label. CORRECTED- the PIC identified and labeled the food as powdered sugar. Ensure all RTE foods that may be mistaken for other foods are labeled once removed to from their original container to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facility in need of repair or cleaning:
1) An accumulation of dust and debris on the shelf above the drive through. Clean nonfood contact surfaces at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
2) Caulking between the hand washing sink and wall in the kitchen.
3) Caulking between the hand washing sink and wall in the mens’ restroom.
4) Caulking between the hand washing sink and wall in the womens’ restroom.
5) Caulking along the back and right side border of the triple sink. 
Physical facilities that may not be moved for cleaning must be adhered to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned and repaired by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

Complete training and test to be made available by the next routine inspection. All High risk establishments should have an Allergen Certified Certified Food Manager within 30 days of employment, to be renewed every 3 years.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed pinto beans in the walk in cooler to be sitting uncovered underneath the cooler’s fans. CORRECTED- a lid was placed on the beans. Ensure all ready to eat (RTE) food items are protected from contamination during storage.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed sanitizer bucket at the front counter to be at a concentration of 0ppm quaternary ammonia (quat). CORRECTED- bucket was remade to 200 ppm. Ensure sanitizer buckets are made at a frequency to hold the sanitizer concentration as recommended by the manufacturer’s label (200-400ppm quat.).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple soda nozzles in both the lobby and drive-thru to contain an accumulation of biofilm. The person in charge (PIC) stated that the soda nozzles are soaked in carbonated water each night. CORRECTED- PIC removed the soda nozzles to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure soda nozzles are both cleaned AND sanitized each night to remove debris that could contaminate RTE beverages. Food contact surfaces must be maintained clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed liquid cheese sauce to have an ambient temperature of 125F, and was probed to have an internal temperature of 126F. CORRECTED- the liquid cheese was voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Liquid cheese was moved to used time as a control for food safety (TAC). The outside of the container was marked with a discard time 4 hours past when the bag was opened. Other options may include using a ladle for liquid cheese until the hot holding unit is serviced or replaced. Hot holding units for hot TCS items must be maintained at or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the Ortega Liquid cheese dispenser to be inadequately holding hot temperatures- see violations #21. Hot holding units must reach temperatures to hold TCS foods at or above 135F. Inspector will return on 10/24/25 to check that the unit is properly hot holding foods. Repair or replace unit.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple incidents of improper utensils storage:
1) Both the chopped tomatoes and onions contained single service bowls with no handles in the food.
2) The ice scoop handle was touching the ice in the drive-thru.
CORRECTED. The single service bowls in the produce were discarded, and the ice scoop was moved to its holder. Scoops with handles should be stored so that the nonfood contact surfaces (the handle, which is touched) is stored above or separate from the food to prevent bare-hand contamination. Do not reuse bowls as scoops, as there is no differentiation between the food-contact surface and the hand contact surface. Either Immediately discard bowl after use, or obtain scoops with handles for produce.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a significant accumulation of burnt food debris on the interior of the quesadilla grill, and grease on the outside of the quesadilla grill. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris. Old food debris could serve as a source of contamination for RTE foods. Inspector will return on 10/24/25 to inspect quesadilla grill cleaning.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of dust on the fans in the walk in cooler. Clean fans at a frequency to prevent potential contamination of foods in storage of the walk in cooler (see violation #15).
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
PIC did not have Allergen training available. They stated they’ve passed it before, but had trouble printing. Allergen training expires every 3 years. Ensure all CFMs take allergen awareness training every 3 years. Maintain records on file to be available upon request during inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed insect trap placed above clean dish ware (on storage rack between office and mop sink). PIC was notified to have pest control company move trap away from food-contact surfaces to prevent contamination. Insect control devices should not be located over areas where food is being prepared, or where clean equipment is being stored. [C]
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspector observed ice bucket faced upwards towards the ceiling- where the food contact surface can be exposed to contaminants.  CORRECTED- Education was provided to the PIC regarding potential contamination of food contact surfaces. Ice bucket was inverted. Food contact surfaces should be stored where they are not exposed to contamination. [C]
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: REPEAT: Cheese sauce dispensed from the Ortega dispenser was observed at 125F (probed). Several portion cups of cheese stored inside the dispenser were observed at 135F (probed). The bag of cheese inside the dispenser has a surface temperature of 135F as indicated using an infrared thermometer. Staff are going to change out the current dispenser for a new one already in the facility. Inspector will follow up tomorrow to see that the new dispenser is functioning properly.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16 (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: PIC is not a certified food protection manager (CFM). Ensure facility is under the supervision of a CFM during all times of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: A food employee was observed to wash hands, turn the faucet off with bare hands, then dry hands with a paper towel. CORRECTED- Discussed proper handwashing with employees. PIC will revisit handwashing procedure with staff. Ensure a paper towel or other barrier is used to turn the faucet off and prevent recontamination of newly cleaned hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12 (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Quat sanitizer in one of the kitchen buckets was observed at 100 ppm quat. CORRECTED- PIC remade the sanitizer solution upon request. Sanitizer was then observed at 200ppm quat. Ensure sanitizer buckets are changed regularly as efficacy declines over time and with use.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall have a concentration as specified on the manufacturer’s label (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Cheese sauce in the Ortega dispenser was observed at 120F (probed) as measured with both inspector’s and facility’s just-calibrated thermometers. CORRECTED- PIC ceased service of the cheese sauce and opened bags in the dispenser were voluntarily discarded. Ensure hot foods are held at 135F or above.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16 (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: The Ortega cheese sauce dispenser is not holding product at 135F or above. Ensure hot holding equipment is sufficient to hold foods at 135F or above.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
1) The backsplash on the soda fountain counter (in the dining room) is not sealed to the countertop itself, with a gap along the bottom edge and apparent water damage. Repair or replace the backsplash, sealing the backsplash to the countertop and to the wall to eliminate any gaps.
2) There is a bare wood observed in the following areas: a) a 4x4 under the dining room soda fountain; b) on the edge of the countertop near the coffee pot; c) behind the tea dispenser; and c) on the edge of the lid shelf near the drive-thru window. Paint or otherwise seal bare wood so it is smooth, easily cleanable, and nonabsorbent.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
PIC has not completed ANSI-approved allergen awareness training. Ensure the facility is under the supervision of a CFM who has completed allergen training during all hours of operation.
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Cheese sauce in the Ortega dispenser was observed at 128F (probed). CORRECTED- PIC ceased service of the cheese sauce, and opened bags in the dispenser were voluntarily discarded. Ensure hot foods are held at 135F or above.
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. [P]

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
Foods on the make line were observed without time markings as required in the facility’s Time as a Control policy. CORRECTED- PIC added time labels indicating when the foods were removed from cold holding. Ensure times are posted and changed when the pans are changed. Ensure foods are used or discarded within 4 hours of being removed from cold holding.
3-501.19: (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
The Ortega cheese sauce dispenser is not holding product at 135F or above. Ensure hot holding equipment is sufficient to hold foods at 135F or above.
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Facility is not equipped with a probe thermometer that can read temperatures below 50F. Ensure a probe thermometer is available that can be used to measure both hot and cold food temperatures.
4-302.12: (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. [Pf]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: PIC has not completed ANSI-approved allergen training. Ensure all CFMs complete ANSI-approved allergen training and keep certificates on file for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]
